And surely the eleven apostles knew that they were planning nothing of the kind against the Lord; but they trust the master more than themselves, and, fearing their own frailty, they sorrowfully ask about a sin of which they had no consciousness.
14:20: But he answered and said: He who dips his hand with me in the dish, he will betray me. O the wonderful patience of the Lord! First he had said: One of you is going to betray me. The betrayer persists in evil; he reproves him more plainly, and yet he does not point out his name specifically. …
14:21:
The Son of Man indeed goes as it is written of him; but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man will be betrayed. Reproved neither the first time nor the second, he does not draw back his foot from the betrayal; rather, he feeds his shamelessness on the patience of the Lord and stores up for himself wrath on the day of wrath. Punishment is foretold, so that the torments announced might correct one whom shame had not overcome. But as to what follows:

 …
14:25: But I say to you: I will not drink from now on of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father. He passes from carnal things to spiritual ones. That the vine transplanted from Egypt is the people of Israel, to whom the Lord speaks through Jeremiah: I planted you a true vine; how have you been changed into the bitterness of a foreign vine, both Isaiah the prophet testifies, in the song which he sings to his beloved, and all Scripture here and there. …
14:26: And when a hymn had been said, they went out to the Mount of Olives. This is what we read in a certain psalm: They have eaten and worshiped, all the fat ones of the earth. According to this example, whoever has been filled and made drunk with the bread and the cup of the Savior can praise the Lord and ascend the Mount of Olives, where there is refreshment from labors, solace for pain, and the knowledge of the true light.
14:27: Then Jesus says to them: All of you will suffer a stumbling block in me on this night. He foretells what they are going to suffer, so that, when they have suffered it, they may not despair of salvation, but may be set free by repenting. And he pointedly added: on this night you will suffer a stumbling block, because, just as those who get drunk get drunk at night, so also those who suffer a stumbling block undergo it in the night and in darkness. But let us say: The night has passed, and the day has drawn near.
14:29: But Peter answered and said to him: Even if all are scandalized, I will never be scandalized. It is not rashness, nor is it a lie; it is the faith of the apostle Peter and his burning affection toward the Lord Savior, of which we spoke above.
14:32: Then Jesus came with them to an estate which is called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples: Sit here while I go over there and pray. Gethsemane is interpreted most fertile valley; there he ordered the disciples to sit for a little while and to wait for his return, while the Lord alone prayed for all.
14:33: And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be saddened and to be sorrowful. What we said above about passion and propassion is shown also in the present passage: that the Lord, in order to prove the reality of the man he had assumed, was indeed truly saddened, but, lest passion should rule in his soul, began to be saddened by way of propassion. For it is one thing to be saddened and another to begin to be saddened. …
14:34: Then he said to them: My soul is sad even to death; stay here and keep watch with me. What is saddened is the soul; and it is saddened not on account of death but even to death, until he should free the apostles by his passion. But as to his command: stay here and keep watch with me, he does not forbid them sleep, for which it was not the time with the danger at hand, but the sleep of unbelief and the torpor of the mind. …
14:37: And he came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he says to Peter: So you could not keep watch with me one hour? He who had said above: Even if all are scandalized in you, I will never be scandalized, now cannot overcome sleep for the greatness of his sadness.
14:39: Again a second time he went away and prayed, saying: My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done. A second time he prays that, if Nineveh cannot be saved otherwise than by the withering of the gourd, the will of the Father may be done, which is not contrary to the will of the Son, as he himself says through the prophet: To do your will, my God, I have willed.
14:4: But the disciples, seeing it, were indignant, saying: To what purpose is this waste? For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor. I know that some cavil at this passage, asking why another evangelist said that Judas alone was saddened, because he held the purse and had been a thief from the beginning, while Matthew writes that all the apostles were indignant; they do not know the figure that is called σύλληψις (syllepsis), by which all are customarily named for one and one for many. …
14:40: And he came again and found them sleeping; for their eyes were heavy. He alone prays for all, just as he alone suffers for all. But the eyes of the apostles were growing faint and weighed down, with the denial near.
14:42: Rise, let us go; behold, he who is going to betray me has drawn near. Let them not find us as though afraid and drawing back; let us go of our own accord to death, so that they may see the confidence and joy of one who is about to suffer.
14:44: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying: Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him. Wretched Judas, and yet not to be pitied! With the same unbelief with which he betrayed his master and Lord, he thought that the signs which he had seen the Savior performing were done not by divine majesty but by magic arts; and because he had perhaps heard that he was transfigured on the mountain, he feared that by a similar transformation he might slip out of the hands of the attendants. …
14:45: And at once coming up to Jesus, he said: Hail, rabbi, and he kissed him. Shameless indeed and wicked is the confidence that calls him master and presses a kiss on the one whom he was betraying. Yet he still has something of a disciple's modesty, since he does not hand him over openly to the persecutors, but through the sign of a kiss. This is the sign which God set on Cain, so that whoever found him should not kill him.
14:47: And behold, one of those who were with Jesus, stretching out his hand, drew his sword, and striking the servant of the chief priest cut off his ear. In another Gospel it is written that Peter did this, with the same ardor of mind as in everything else. The servant of the chief priest, too, is called Malchus; and the ear that is cut off is the right one. …
14:48: At that hour Jesus said: You have come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to arrest me? Daily I sat among you teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me. It is foolish, he says, to seek with swords and clubs one who hands himself over of his own accord into your hands, and to track down at night through a betrayer, as if he were hiding and avoiding your eyes, one who teaches daily in the temple. But you gather against me in darkness for this reason, that your power is in darkness.
14:49: But all this was done that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. What are the Scriptures of the prophets? They pierced my hands and feet; and elsewhere: He was led like a sheep to the sacrifice; and in another place: By the iniquities of my people he was led to death.
14:53: But they, holding Jesus, led him to Caiaphas the chief priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered. Moses, at God's command, had ordered that the high priests should succeed their fathers and that a line of descent should be woven among the priests. Josephus relates that this Caiaphas bought the high priesthood for one year only from Herod for a price. It is no wonder, then, if an unjust high priest judges unjustly.
14:54: And going inside he sat with the attendants, to see the end. Either out of a disciple's love or out of human curiosity he wished to know what the high priest would decide about the Lord: whether he would condemn him to death or would release him after beating him with scourges. And in this lies the difference between the ten apostles and Peter: they flee; he, although from a distance, still follows the Savior.
14:57: At last two false witnesses came and said: This man said: I can destroy the temple of God and after three days build it. How are they false witnesses, if they say the things which we read above that the Lord said? But a false witness is one who does not understand what is said in the same sense in which it is said. For the Lord had spoken of the temple of his body; but they falsely accuse him in the very words too, and by adding or changing a few they make, as it were, a just accusation. …
14:6: When the apostles pleaded that the ointment was being wasted, they were rebuked by the voice of the Lord. Christ did not need the ointment, nor do martyrs need the light of candles. Yet that woman freely poured out the ointment in honor of Christ, and her heart's devotion was accepted.… Hence throughout the whole Eastern Church, even when there are no relics of the martyrs, whenever the gospel is to be read the candles are lighted although the dawn may be reddening the sky, not of course to scatter the darkness, …
14:60: And the chief priest, rising up, said to him: Do you answer nothing to the things these men testify against you? But Jesus was silent. Headlong anger and impatience, finding no ground for a false accusation, shake the high priest from his throne, so that he might show the madness of his mind by the movement of his body. …
14:61: And the chief priest said to him: I adjure you by the living God that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God. Why do you adjure him, most impious of priests: in order to accuse, or in order to believe? If in order to accuse, others are accusing him: condemn him in his silence; if in order to believe, why did you refuse to believe him when he confessed?
14:63: Then the chief priest tore his garments, saying: He has blasphemed; what further need have we of witnesses? The man whom fury had shaken from the priestly throne the same rage provokes to tear his clothes. And he tears his garments to show that the Jews had lost the glory of the priesthood and that the high priests have an empty seat. …
14:7: But Jesus, knowing it, said to them: Why do you trouble the woman? She has wrought a good work on me; for you always have the poor with you, but me you will not always have. Another question arises: why the Lord said to the disciples after the resurrection: Behold, I am with you even to the consummation of the world, and now says: but me you will not always have. …
14:70: Surely you too are one of them, for your speech also makes you plain. Not that Peter was of another language or of a foreign nation, for all of them were Hebrews, both those who accused and he who was accused, but because each province and region had its own peculiarities and could not avoid its native sound of speech. Hence too the Ephraimites in the book of Judges cannot say the σύνθημα (the password).
14:71: Then he began to curse and to swear that he did not know the man. And immediately the cock crowed. In another Gospel we read that after Peter's denial and the crowing of the cock the Savior looked at Peter and by his gaze moved him to bitter tears; nor could it be that he should remain in the darkness of denial on whom the light of the world had looked.
14:8: For in putting this ointment on my body, she has done it for my burial. What you think to be a waste of ointment is the office of burial. Nor is it strange if she has given me the good odor of her faith, since I am going to pour out my blood for her.
15:1: When morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, to hand him over to death; and they led him bound and handed him over to Pontius Pilate the governor. He was led not only to Pilate but also to Herod, so that both might mock the Lord. And see the zeal of the priests for evil: they kept watch the whole night in order to commit murder. And they handed him over bound to Pilate. …
15:15: Then he released Barabbas to them; but Jesus, scourged, he handed over to them to be crucified. Barabbas the robber, who stirred up seditions among the crowds, who was the author of murders, was released to the people of the Jews, that is, the devil, who reigns in them to this day, and for that reason they cannot have peace; but Jesus, handed over by the Jews, is acquitted by Pilate's wife and is called just by the governor himself, and the centurion confesses that he is truly the Son of God. …
15:16: Then the soldiers of the governor, taking Jesus into the praetorium, gathered the whole cohort to him; and stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak around him, and plaiting a crown of thorns they put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand, and bending the knee before him they mocked him, saying: Hail, king of the Jews. …
15:19: And spitting on him they took the reed and struck his head. At that time was fulfilled: I did not turn away my face from the shame of spitting. And yet, though they strike his head with a reed, he bears all things patiently, to show true the prophecy of Isaiah, who says: A shaken reed he will not break.
15:2: Jesus says to him: You say so. He answered in such a way that he both spoke the truth and his word lay open to no false accusation. And note that to Pilate, who was pronouncing sentence unwillingly, he answered in some part, but to the priests and rulers he would not answer, judging them unworthy of his speech.
15:22: And they came to the place which is called Golgotha, which is the place of Calvary. I have heard someone expound the place of Calvary as the place in which Adam was buried, and say that it was so called because the head of the ancient man was laid there, and that this is what the Apostle says: Arise, you who sleep, and rise from the dead, and Christ will enlighten you. A pleasing interpretation, and soothing to the ear of the people, but not true. …
15:27: Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left. If Golgotha is the tomb of Adam and not the place of the condemned, and the Lord is crucified there in order to raise up Adam, why are two robbers crucified in the same place?
15:29: And those passing by blasphemed him, moving their heads. They blasphemed because they were passing by the way and would not walk on the true road of the Scriptures. They moved their heads because they had already moved their feet before and did not stand upon the rock. And the foolish people, insulting him, says the very same thing that the false witnesses had made up.
15:35: But some who were standing there and heard it said: This man is calling Elijah. Not all, but some, whom I judge to have been Roman soldiers who did not understand the idiom of the Hebrew language, but from the fact that he said: Heli Heli, thought that Elijah was being invoked by him. But if you would rather understand that it was Jews who said this, they do this too in their usual manner, to defame the Lord with weakness, as one who begs the help of Elijah.
15:37: And Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, sent forth his spirit. It is a sign of divine power to send forth the spirit, as he himself had also said: No one can take my soul from me, but I lay it down of myself, that I may take it up again.
15:38: And the veil of the temple was torn in two, from the top to the bottom. The veil of the temple was torn, and all the mysteries of the law, which were previously covered, were laid open and passed over to the people of the Gentiles. In the Gospel of which we often make mention, we read that the lintel of the temple, of immense size, was broken and split apart. Josephus also reports that the angelic powers, once the guardians of the temple, then cried out together: Let us depart from these abodes.
15:46: And having taken the body of Jesus, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth. From the simple burial of the Lord the ambition of the rich is condemned, who cannot do without riches even in their tombs. And according to spiritual understanding we can also take this to mean that the body of the Lord is to be wrapped not in gold, not in gems and silk, but in pure linen; although this too may be signified, that he wraps Jesus in a clean linen cloth who has received him with a pure mind.
15:47: And Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the sepulcher. While the others left the Lord, the women persevere in their duty, waiting for what Jesus had promised; and therefore they deserved to be the first to see him rising, because he who perseveres to the end, he shall be saved.
15:5: Do you not hear how many testimonies they speak against you? But Jesus would answer nothing, lest by refuting the charge he should be released by the governor and the benefit of the cross be put off.
15:7: Now he had at that time a notable prisoner, who was called Barabbas. This man, in the Gospel which is written according to the Hebrews, is interpreted as son of their master; he had been condemned for sedition and murder.
15:9: Pilate offers them the choice of whom they wished him to release, the robber or Jesus, not doubting that Jesus would rather be chosen, since he knew that he had been handed over out of envy. Therefore the cause of the cross is plainly envy.
16:4: And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, and coming up he rolled back the stone and was sitting upon it; and his appearance was like lightning, and his clothing like snow. Our Lord, one and the same Son of God and Son of Man, according to each nature, of divinity and of flesh, shows now the signs of his greatness, now those of his lowliness. …
1:13: And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward he was hungry. In this number the mystery of the forty days is shown to us, in which Moses too fasted on Mount Sinai and Elijah beside Mount Horeb. But the body is allowed to be hungry so that the devil may be given the occasion to tempt.
1:14: From then on Jesus began to preach and to say: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven will draw near. With John handed over, he himself rightly begins to preach. As the law ceases, the Gospel accordingly arises. And if the Savior preaches the same things that John the Baptist had said before, he shows that he is the Son of the same God whose prophet the latter is.
1:17: Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men. These were the first called to follow the Lord; fishermen and unlettered men are sent to preach, lest the faith of believers be thought to come about not by the power of God but by eloquence and learning.
1:2: For this is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah, saying: The voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. He was preparing the souls of believers, in which the Lord was going to walk, so that he, the pure one, might walk in most pure ways, saying: I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. …
1:20: There must have been something divinely compelling in the face of the Savior. Otherwise they would not have acted so irrationally as to follow a man whom they had never seen before. Does one leave a father to follow a man in whom he sees nothing more than he sees in his father? They left their father of the flesh to follow the Father of the spirit. They did not leave a father; they found a Father. What is the point of this digression? …
1:22: And he was teaching them as one having authority, not as the scribes. For they taught the peoples the things that are written in Moses and the prophets, but Jesus, as God and Lord of Moses himself, by the freedom of his own will either added in the law the things that seemed lacking or, changing them, preached to the peoples, as we also read above: It was said to the ancients; but I say to you.
1:30: Can you imagine Jesus standing before your bed and you continue sleeping? It is absurd that you would remain in bed in his presence. Where is Jesus? He is already here offering himself to us. "In the middle," he says, "among you he stands, whom you do not recognize." "The kingdom of God is in your midst." Faith beholds Jesus among us. If we are unable to seize his hand, let us prostrate ourselves at his feet. If we are unable to reach his head, let us wash his feet with our tears. …
1:31: When Jesus had come into Peter's house, he saw his mother-in-law lying ill with fever, and he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she rose and served them. The woman's hand is touched, and as her works are healed the infirmity of sins flees. Human nature is such that after a fever bodies are the more wearied, and as health begins they feel the ills of the sickness. …
1:32: When evening had come, they brought to him many who had demons, and he cast out the spirits with a word and healed all who were ill. All are healed not in the morning, not at midday, but towards evening, when the sun is about to set, when the grain of wheat dies in the earth that it may bear much fruit.
1:44: But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them. He sends him to the priest for various reasons. First, for humility's sake, that he may be seen to defer to the priests. For it was commanded in the law that those who had been cleansed of leprosy should offer gifts to the priests. …
1:5: The baptism of John did not so much consist in the forgiveness of sins as in being a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, that is, for a future remission, which was to follow through the sanctification of Christ.
1:8: He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire. Either because the Holy Spirit is fire, as the Acts of the Apostles teach, at whose descent there sat as it were fire upon the tongues of the believers, and the word of the Lord was fulfilled who said: I came to send fire upon the earth, and how I wish that it may burn; or because in the present we are baptized with the spirit and in the future with fire, the Apostle too agreeing with this sense: The fire will test what sort each one's work is.
1:9: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him. For a threefold reason the Savior received baptism from John: first, so that, since he had been born a man, he might fulfill all the justice and humility of the law; second, so that by his own baptism he might approve the baptism of John; third, so that, sanctifying the waters of the Jordan by the descent of the dove, he might show the coming of the Holy Spirit in the washing of believers.
2:15: And it came to pass, as he reclined at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Jesus, and the rest. They had seen that a tax collector converted from sins to better things had found a place of repentance, and on that account they too do not despair of salvation; nor indeed do they come to Jesus remaining in their former vices, as the Pharisees and scribes murmur, but repenting, as the Lord's following word signifies, saying:
2:19: Jesus said to them: Can the sons of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast. The bridegroom is Christ, the bride is the Church. From this holy and spiritual marriage the apostles were begotten, who cannot mourn as long as they see the bride in the bridal chamber and know that the bridegroom is with the bride. …
2:24: But the Pharisees, seeing it, said to him: Behold, your disciples are doing what it is not lawful for them to do on the Sabbaths. Note that the first apostles of the Savior destroy the letter of the Sabbath, against the Ebionites, who, though they receive the other apostles, reject Paul as a transgressor of the law.
2:3: And, as we said above, they brought to him a second paralytic, lying on a little bed, because he himself was not able to walk in. And Jesus, seeing the faith, not of the one who was being brought but of those who were bringing him, said to the paralytic: Take heart, son, your sins are forgiven you. O wonderful humility! He calls son one who was despised and infirm and loosened in all the joints of his limbs, one whom the priests did not deign to touch. …
2:6: And behold, some of the scribes said within themselves: This man blasphemes. We read in the prophet, God saying: I am he who blots out your iniquities. Consistently, therefore, the scribes, because they thought him a man and understood the words of God, accuse him of blasphemy. …
2:9: Which is easier, to say: Your sins are forgiven you; or to say: Rise and walk? Between saying and doing there is a great distance. Whether the sins had been forgiven the paralytic, he alone knew who was forgiving them. Rise, however, and walk could be verified as much by him who was rising as by those who saw him rise. A bodily sign therefore is wrought so that the spiritual one may be proved, although it belongs to the same power to remit the faults both of body and of soul. …
3:1: And when he had passed on from there, he came into their synagogue. And behold, a man having a withered hand. This man, who is healed in the synagogue, is the thirteenth. And it is to be noted that the hand was withered not on the road and out of doors, but in the assembly of the Jews.
3:2: And they questioned him, saying: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbaths? so that they might accuse him. Since he had excused by an acceptable example the destruction of the Sabbath which the Pharisees charged against the disciples, they wish to slander him himself, and they ask whether it is lawful to heal on the Sabbaths, so that, if he did not heal, they might accuse him of cruelty or of weakness, and if he healed, of transgression.
3:21: In the gospel we read that even his kinsfolk desired to bind him as one of weak mind. His opponents also reviled him saying, "You are a Samaritan and have a devil."
3:22: But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them: Every kingdom divided within itself will be laid waste. The crowds were amazed and confessed that he who did such great signs was the son of David; but the Pharisees ascribed the works of God to the prince of the demons; and the Lord answered them not according to what they said but according to what they thought, so that even thus they might be compelled to believe in the power of him who saw the hidden things of the heart.
3:6: But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him. That they lay plots against the Lord, envy is the cause. For what had he done to provoke the Pharisees to kill him? Why, that a man had stretched out his hand. For which of the Pharisees does not stretch out his hand on the Sabbath day, carrying food, holding out a cup, and the other things that are necessary for living? …
3:7: But Jesus, knowing it, withdrew from there. Knowing their plots, that they wished to destroy their Savior, he withdrew from there, so as to take away from the Pharisees an occasion for impiety against himself.
4:11: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see and hearing they do not hear. He says these things of those who stand on the shore and are separated from Jesus, and, with the sound of the waves roaring, do not hear clearly what is said, and in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah: By hearing you shall hear and shall not understand, and seeing you shall see and shall not see. These things were prophesied of the crowds that stand on the shore and do not deserve to hear the word of God. …
4:15: The evil one comes and snatches what has been sown in his heart. The evil one snatches the good seed. And at the same time understand that it was sown in the heart, and that the different kinds of ground are the souls of believers.
4:17: But when tribulation and persecution have come because of the word, he is at once scandalized. Pay attention to what is said: he is at once scandalized. There is therefore some difference between the one who is compelled by many tribulations and punishments to deny Christ and the one who at the first persecution is immediately scandalized and falls.
4:30: The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field; which indeed is the least of all seeds, but when it has grown it is greater than all garden herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and dwell in its branches. Let it not be irksome to the reader if we set out whole parables. For things that are obscure must be discussed more fully, lest by excessive brevity the sense be wrapped up rather than explained. …
4:36: And as he went up into the boat his disciples followed him, and the rest. The fifth sign he did when, going up into the ship from Capernaum, he commanded the winds and the sea; the sixth, when in the country of the Gerasenes he gave the demons power over the swine; the seventh, when, entering his own city, he healed the second paralytic on his bed; for the first paralytic is the centurion's servant.
4:38: But he was sleeping. And they came and woke him, saying: Lord, save us. The type of this sign we read in Jonah, when, while the others are in peril, he himself is untroubled and sleeps, and is woken, and by the command and mystery of his passion frees those who woke him.
4:39: Then rising he rebuked the winds and the sea. And from this place we understand that all creatures perceive the Creator. For the things that are rebuked and commanded perceive the one who commands, not by the error of the heretics, who think all things are animate, but by the majesty of the Maker, to whom things insensible to us are sensible.
4:9: He who has ears to hear, let him hear. We are roused to the understanding of what is said whenever we are admonished by these words.
5:17: And behold, the whole city went out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him they asked him to pass from their borders. Those who ask him to pass beyond their borders do this not from pride (as some suppose) but from humility, by which they judged themselves unworthy of the Lord's presence, just as Peter too, at the catch of fish, falling at the Savior's knees, says: Go out from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man.
5:25: There were many who kept promising that way which would lead to the city. Socrates promised, Plato promised, Aristotle promised. The woman with the issue of blood, who flowed with blood, sought many physicians, and by none could be healed. "They did not find the way of the city of habitation." Their teaching produced hunger for the truth rather than fullness. The woman with the issue of blood spent all her substance on physicians: hungering and thirsting her soul failed within her. …
5:28: For she said within herself: If I only touch the fringe of his garment, I shall be well. According to the law, whoever touches a menstruous woman or one with a flow of blood is unclean. She touches the Lord for this reason, that she too may be healed of the fault of her blood.
5:33: Note the separate stages; mark the progress. As long as she was hemorrhaging, she could not come into his presence. She was healed by faith and then came before him. She fell at his feet. Even then she did not yet dare to look up into his face. As long as she had been cured, it was enough for her to cling to his feet. She "told him all the truth." Christ himself is the truth. She was giving praise to the truth. She had been healed by the truth.
5:37: Someone may wonder or ask: Why are these three apostles always chosen and the others sent away? Even when he was transfigured on the mountain, these three were with him. Yes, these three were chosen: Peter, James and John. But why only three? First there is the mystery of the Trinity embedded in this number, a number sacred in itself.
